A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H support comparison, including the additional theoretical material in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on Cartpole, Inventory Management, and 3-D Inventory Management, including robustness tests and appendix schedule comparisons.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments, with numerical results in Tables 2–4 and 11–12 and training and testing curves in Figures 1–18.

M1.justification: V3 adds a non-rectangular inner solver: Algorithm 2 combines Approximate TMA with conservative policy iteration, a Frank–Wolfe gap stopping criterion, and mixture updates to transition kernels. Algorithm 1 also changes its direct update's search domain from the probability simplex to the uncertainty set P. The existing practical MDPO implementation is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three domains and their constrained, unconstrained, robust, and non-robust variants under the same distortion scenarios. The non-rectangular extension adds theory, not an evaluated task or environment.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 and 11–12 retain the same evaluated MCPMD, PPO, and MDPO variants and schedule comparators. Added comparisons with prior theoretical guarantees in Table 1 are not new empirical baselines.

E3.justification: The short and long training budgets, distortion testing procedures, evaluation counts, return and penalised-return metrics, and experimental configurations remain unchanged. Appendix E retains the same architectures, optimisers, and hyperparameters.

E4.justification: The robustness and constraint-component comparisons, training analyses, and larger-budget tests are retained. Appendix H already contained the fixed, linear, restart, and geometric schedule comparisons highlighted more prominently in v3.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same ten-seed experiments, training-curve standard errors, environment-based test standard errors, and pooled-standard-error highlighting rule. No repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation practice changes.

E6.justification: The empirical entries in Tables 2–4 and 11–12 match, and the plotted graphics in Figures 1–18 are unchanged. The reported empirical rankings, sample-efficiency findings, and constraint-satisfaction outcomes are retained.

T1.justification: New Section 5.5 introduces the TMA–policy-iteration relation, a non-rectangularity measure delta_P, and Theorem 3's O(epsilon + delta_P) average-regret guarantee with O-tilde(epsilon^(-5)) samples, supported by Appendix D.6.3. V3 also expands v2 Lemma 23 into Lemma 24's general and norm-bounded cases, revises Theorem 2's conditions, and corrects several Approximate TMA and appendix derivations.

C1.justification: The introduction, Table 1, and conclusion expand the central theoretical contribution to non-rectangular RCMDPs, claiming an O-tilde(T^(-1/5)) rate with the residual error specified in Theorem 3. The rectangular O-tilde(T^(-1/3)) claim and empirical performance claims are retained.

C2.justification: V3 explains statistical advantages of non-rectangular sets alongside their slower convergence and residual non-rectangularity error. It also reframes tight norm-bounded uncertainty sets as improving constants rather than being essential to the convergence rate. Empirical interpretations and the acknowledged practical–theoretical implementation gap remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the same implementation instructions, hyperparameter tables, software, CPU usage, runtime information, and code-access references. Changing the critic description from 'heads' to 'outputs' matches the already documented Linear(1+m) architecture rather than disclosing a new implementation.

R1.justification: Sections 2.2–2.3 and Table 1 substantially expand positioning against rectangular and non-rectangular RMDP theory, distinguishing oracle and sample guarantees and exact versus residual-error convergence. V3 develops its relationship to Li et al. (2023) and Wang et al. (2024), and adds Kumar et al. (2025).

P1.justification: The introduction gains structured theoretical and experimental contribution lists, related-work paragraphs are substantially rewritten, and the preliminaries expand explanations of regret and optimisation objectives. Terminology and the theoretical narrative are clarified throughout, beyond the insertion of the new scientific section.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned with an MDP-type column and revised rows, and a new Algorithm 2 display is added. Existing floats move relative to surrounding text, and several appendix captions are shortened. The empirical plots and result-table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 improves exposition and corrects several equations. However, its expanded guarantees depend on Lemma 24, which retains v2 Lemma 23's unjustified removal of value-dependent weights before telescoping signed transition differences. The resulting unweighted sums cancel by probability normalization and do not justify the weighted bound in Appendix D.6.1. Extending the claims without repairing this central proof gap leaves the net quality effect uncertain, despite clear local corrections and unchanged empirical evidence.
